## Capital Region Jeonse Loan Restrictions

Starting next year, the government is implementing sweeping restrictions on jeonse loans for single-property owners in the Seoul metropolitan area who have never actually lived in their apartments. The policy aims to curb speculative housing practices where investors leverage jeonse deposits to purchase properties while living elsewhere as tenants. The government is reducing jeonse loan guarantee ratios by 10 percentage points, from 80 to 90 percent down to 70 to 80 percent. While the measure targets speculation, it includes exceptions for owners who have any residential history in the property, even just one day, or those facing unavoidable circumstances like unable-to-occupy situations due to existing tenants.

## Non-Apartment Deregulation Initiative

To address the escalating jeonse crisis, the government is loosening regulations on non-apartment housing including multi-unit villas and officetel buildings. The comprehensive housing supply plan unveiled on August 13th exempts small non-apartment new construction purchases from household count calculations while rationalizing building standards to accelerate supply. The government is introducing a universal six-year public rental housing program and affordable public ownership options where residents can purchase homes with just 25 percent down payment while gradually increasing equity stakes. These measures represent a shift from apartment-centric policy to embrace diverse housing types that can serve lower-income households more effectively.

## Seoul Land Auction Modest Results

The government's highly anticipated land auction in Seoul yielded only 1,000 households worth of housing, forcing accelerated focus on redevelopment and reconstruction projects instead. The comprehensive supply plan targets 230,000 households from multiple initiatives, with 100,000 units planned for new development sites in the capital region, specifically in Namyangju and Gwangju by 2030. While greenbelts in areas like Naegok, Suseo, and Bangi are expected to be deregulated, the government has not yet formally announced specific locations, instead presenting aggregate supply figures of 73,000 plus additional units. This cautious approach reflects the complexity of land policy negotiations and environmental concerns surrounding greenbelts.

## Semiconductor Cluster Regulatory Relief

Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul announced ambitious plans to unlock stalled industrial investments, particularly in the Pohang industrial complex and semiconductor cluster development. The government is relaxing construction law regulations that previously required separate permits for each factory expansion, enabling early implementation of two trillion won in planned investments. Specifically, the Yongin semiconductor cluster is expected to accelerate its development timeline by seven years through streamlined permitting. This regulatory overhaul responds to intensifying global competition in memory semiconductor production, as companies worldwide race to increase capacity amid persistent chip shortages.

## First-Time Homebuyers Housing Support

Starting January next year, young adults earning less than 70 million won annually can purchase non-apartment housing under 400 million won with down payments covering just 20 percent of the property value, borrowing up to 80 percent through the new Youth Future Housing Loan program. The financial authorities are introducing a comprehensive three-part support package including purchase financing, semi-jeonse, and full jeonse loans with expanded limits specifically targeting young people and newlyweds. Monthly repayment amounts are calibrated to match typical rental rates, making homeownership more accessible. This pinpoint support strategy distinguishes between legitimate end-users and speculative investors, protecting real estate market stability while enabling genuine housing demand.

## First-Half Fiscal Deficit Improves

The government's fiscal position strengthened significantly in the first half of 2026, with the structural budget deficit reaching 84 trillion won, the lowest level in three years. Total government revenues jumped 61.3 trillion won or 19.1 percent year-over-year to 381.9 trillion won, driven by 33 trillion won in increased national tax revenue. Income tax collections rose 10.4 trillion won due to performance bonus payments and increased real estate transactions, while corporate taxes grew 4.3 trillion won from improved business results. However, increased expenditures for health insurance support, local education financing, and consumer recovery coupons continue straining fiscal resources, requiring careful budget management going forward.

## US Disinflationary Signals Emerge

American inflation cooled to 3.4 percent in July, down from previous months, weakening the Federal Reserve's rationale for additional rate increases. Market expectations have shifted dramatically, with Chicago Mercantile Exchange's FedWatch tool now showing 60 percent probability the Fed will hold rates steady at its September meeting, up significantly from prior forecasts of rate hikes. The disinflationary trend signals a potential inflection point in US economic momentum, as the Fed's aggressive monetary tightening appears to be gaining traction. However, bond markets remain cautious, with ten-year Treasury auction yields reaching post-financial crisis highs, reflecting persistent inflation concerns and geopolitical uncertainties.

## Kospi Gains on Semiconductor Strength

The Kospi index surged into the 6500 range, maintaining gains of 3 to 4 percent over four consecutive trading sessions, driven primarily by semiconductor sector strength. The Kosdaq advanced 0.29 percent to 861.37, also marking its fourth day of gains as foreign investors and institutions returned to buying stocks. The Korean won strengthened 3.7 won against the dollar to 1,419.4 won, reflecting improved sentiment toward Korean assets. This rally reflects growing optimism that the US Federal Reserve will maintain accommodative policy, benefiting technology-heavy portfolios and semiconductor exporters.

## LG Energy Solution Resumes Production

LG Energy Solution and General Motors' battery joint venture Ultium Cells is restarting its Ohio factory operations just seven months after shutting down due to weakening electric vehicle demand. The resumption reflects recovery in EV market fundamentals and rising international crude oil prices, which improve the economic case for electric vehicles against combustion engines. LG Energy Solution is also seeing improved capacity utilization across its domestic and international battery plants, signaling renewed confidence in long-term EV adoption trajectories despite near-term market softness.

## Semiconductor and Secondary Battery Deregulation

The government is systematically eliminating regulatory barriers in semiconductors, secondary batteries, and biotechnology sectors, expecting to generate 4.2 trillion won in new investment effects. Recognizing battery recycling as a core manufacturing process, authorities are lowering entry barriers for facility operators to support 100 billion won in fresh private investment. The biotech sector benefits from expanded manufacturing facility extensions at the Ochang Science Industrial Complex. These deregulation measures acknowledge that Korea's advanced technology sectors face intense global competition and require streamlined development processes to maintain competitive advantage against rivals in the United States, Taiwan, and Europe.

## Naver Invests in Wave-Powered Data Centers

Naver is expanding AI infrastructure investments beyond traditional computing capacity by investing in Panthalassa, a US startup developing wave-powered floating data centers. The 2016-founded company is pioneering sustainable offshore AI infrastructure that generates continuous electricity through wave energy without requiring separate power plants or fuel. The floating node platforms integrate power generation, AI computation and processing, and cooling functions in single units, dramatically reducing land acquisition costs compared to traditional terrestrial data centers. This strategic investment positions Naver to secure long-term competitive advantages in AI infrastructure while advancing environmental sustainability objectives.

## South Korea-US Auto Tariff Tensions

American auto dealership associations are publicly urging the Trump administration to implement comprehensive barriers against Chinese vehicle market entry, citing successful Chinese penetration of European markets despite punitive tariffs. The US currently maintains unprecedented 127.5 percent tariffs on Chinese vehicles, effectively blocking market entry, yet dealerships are requesting strengthened protectionist measures beyond current tariff levels. This escalation reflects concerns about Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers' successful navigation of EU tariff barriers, suggesting that sustained high tariffs may prove insufficient to prevent competitive threats. The dealership industry's unified position underscores how rapidly Chinese automotive capabilities are advancing globally.

## Manufacturing Supply Chain AI Adoption

Survey data shows that 91.5 percent of South Korea's largest 200 manufacturing companies recognize supply chain-wide artificial intelligence transformation as essential for competitive strength. Expected benefits include productivity improvements at 48.8 percent, supply chain risk mitigation at 22.9 percent, and cost reduction at 19.6 percent. However, 45 percent of surveyed companies have already begun supporting supplier AI adoption, facing primary constraints from supplier digital infrastructure and AI capability deficiencies. This finding indicates that Korea's manufacturing competitiveness increasingly depends on ecosystem-wide technological advancement, requiring coordinated industry and government support for supplier digitalization.

## K-Beauty Export Momentum

Able C&C achieved 53 percent operating profit growth in the second quarter, capitalizing on accelerating Korean beauty industry global expansion. Export proportions in cosmetics operations expanded from 50.34 percent in 2024 to 53.59 percent in 2025 and 69.80 percent in the first half of 2026, demonstrating consistent internationalization momentum. The company has established local subsidiaries across 56 countries including Japan, the United States, and China, positioning itself at the forefront of the K-beauty phenomenon. This success exemplifies how Korean companies are leveraging global consumer preferences and supply chain advantages to capture expanding international markets, particularly among younger demographics worldwide.

## Investment Implications

For individual investors, the government's multi-pronged housing support strategy and regulatory relief measures suggest sustained policy commitment to stabilizing real estate markets while managing inflation. The improved fiscal position despite increased spending demonstrates strong tax revenue growth, supporting confidence in government financial sustainability. In equity markets, semiconductor sector strength coupled with infrastructure AI investments offers compelling opportunities as global chip demand accelerates and data center buildouts accelerate. The 4 percent Kospi gains reflect foreign investor confidence in Korean technology stocks amid moderating US inflation expectations. However, given US Treasury yields at post-crisis highs and persistent international uncertainties, diversified portfolio positioning remains prudent through the September Fed decision. Young investors should note expanded first-time homebuyer programs offering unprecedented leverage at favorable terms, fundamentally improving residential property accessibility.
